questions.q: What does the webservice keyword do when applied to an Apex method?
options: It exposes the method as a custom SOAP web service operation that an external application can invoke
It marks the method as an HttpCalloutMock for testing
It schedules the method to run nightly
It registers the method as a Platform Event subscriber
questions.explain: The webservice keyword publishes an Apex method as a custom SOAP operation, letting an external application invoke it to perform an action in Salesforce.

questions.q: What two requirements must be true for a webservice method to work?
options: The method must be private, and the class must be public
The method must be static, and the containing class must be global
The method must implement Queueable, and the class must implement Database.Batchable
The method must be annotated @HttpPost, and the class must use @RestResource
questions.explain: A webservice method must be static, and the class containing it must be declared global — the keyword cannot be used on classes, interfaces, interface members, or triggers.

questions.q: How does an external developer get the information needed to build a SOAP client against a custom Apex web service?
options: By reading the Apex debug log
By generating the WSDL from the class in Setup (Apex Classes > the class > Generate WSDL) and using it to build a matching client
SOAP clients require no description document at all
By calling the standard REST API's describe endpoint
questions.explain: The WSDL document, generated from the Apex class in Setup, describes the operation's parameters and types so an external SOAP client can be built correctly.

questions.q: Why does this lesson say SOAP web services in Apex still matter despite being a legacy mechanism?
options: Because SOAP is faster than REST in every case
Because some older enterprise systems (legacy ERPs, older middleware) were built against SOAP and have no practical path to switching protocols
Because Apex REST cannot be used with Named Credentials
Because the webservice keyword is required for all Platform Event publishing
questions.explain: The practical justification is integrating with existing systems that genuinely cannot consume REST/JSON and require a SOAP contract instead.

questions.q: Per this lesson's comparison, when should a developer reach for the webservice keyword instead of Apex REST for a brand-new integration?
options: Always — SOAP should be the default choice for all new work
Only when the external caller is a legacy system that genuinely cannot consume REST/JSON and requires a SOAP contract
Never — the webservice keyword has been fully removed from Apex
Only when the integration needs to exceed 100 callouts per transaction
questions.explain: Apex REST is the default recommendation for callers that can speak REST/JSON; SOAP is reserved for callers that specifically cannot.
